flashcards.q: State Cloud Logging's ingestion pricing, free tier, and retention rules.
flashcards.a: $0.50/GiB ingested, 50 GiB/month free per project. That charge includes 30 days of storage; extended retention beyond 30 days costs an additional $0.01/GiB-month.

flashcards.q: How do Cloud Logging exclusion filters save money, and what happens if the log is also exported via a sink?
flashcards.a: An exclusion filter stops a log from being ingested/billed at Logging's $0.50/GiB rate entirely. If a separate sink still exports that same log to Pub/Sub, GCS, or BigQuery, the export proceeds normally -- you pay that destination's (usually much cheaper) rate instead of Logging's ingestion charge.

flashcards.q: Name the four Cloud Audit Log types and which are free vs chargeable.
flashcards.a: Admin Activity (free, always on, can't disable) and System Event (free, Google-initiated actions) form the _Required bucket with free 400-day retention. Data Access (chargeable, off by default except a few services -- biggest cost-spike risk) and Policy Denied (chargeable, on by default) land in regular chargeable buckets.

flashcards.q: How is an error budget calculated, and what does a 99.9% SLO over 30 days yield?
flashcards.a: Error budget = (1 - SLO target) applied to the compliance period. A 99.9% availability SLO over 30 days yields roughly 43.2 minutes of allowed downtime for the period.

flashcards.q: What is a burn-rate alert and why does it beat a static error-rate threshold?
flashcards.a: Fires when X% of the error budget is consumed within a lookback window (default ~60 min), measuring consumption speed relative to a sustainable pace. Unlike a static threshold, it accounts for REMAINING budget -- avoiding both alert fatigue (firing on budget-cheap noise) and missed slow-burn incidents (steady degradation that never spikes dramatically).

flashcards.q: Describe a standard tiered burn-rate alerting setup.
flashcards.a: Fast-burn (e.g. 10x rate, exhausting the month's budget in ~3 days if sustained) pages on-call immediately. Slow-burn (e.g. 2x rate, longer lookback window) opens a ticket rather than paging -- catches gradual degradation a short fast-burn lookback would miss.

flashcards.q: State Cloud Trace pricing and contrast head-based vs tail-based sampling.
flashcards.a: 2.5M spans/month free, $0.20/million beyond -- near-free at typical scale, so sampling strategy is driven by signal quality, not cost. Head-based: fixed rate (5-10% typical), decision made before outcome known, cuts volume ~90% but drops a proportional share of errors. Tail-based: decision deferred until full trace seen, keeps errors/slow outliers preferentially -- needs an OpenTelemetry Collector, not native to Cloud Trace.

flashcards.q: What are Sustained Use Discounts (SUDs) and which machine families are eligible?
flashcards.a: Automatic, zero-commitment discount up to 30% off, applied once a VM runs more than 25% of the billing month. Only N1, N2, N2D, C2, M1, M2 are eligible -- E2, C3, C4, N4, and all accelerator-optimized families are explicitly excluded. No AWS/Azure equivalent (their discounts always require a commitment).

flashcards.q: State CUD terms and the 2026 scope change.
flashcards.a: Commit vCPU+memory in a region for 1 year (37% off) or 3 years (55% off), no-upfront-payment only (unlike AWS RIs which offer All/Partial-Upfront for deeper discounts). 2026 update: default scope moved from per-project to billing-account, so one commitment can apply across projects, fixing the classic stranded-commitment problem when one project's usage shrinks.

flashcards.q: What is the key limitation of the GCP CUD Recommender?
flashcards.a: It suggests coverage based on recent usage patterns but does not model growth uncertainty or protect against usage dropping after commitment -- a good free starting signal for early-stage FinOps, not a substitute for judgment-based sizing. Size commitments conservatively below historical minimum usage, not the raw recommendation.

flashcards.topic: GCP vs AWS Logging Free Tier
flashcards.q: Compare Cloud Logging's and CloudWatch Logs' free tiers and per-GB rates.
flashcards.a: Both charge roughly $0.50/GB ingestion. Cloud Logging's free tier is 50 GiB/month; CloudWatch Logs' free tier is only 5 GB/month -- a 10x difference giving GCP more headroom before logging costs become material at the same volume, though at high volume the deciding cost factor is operational hygiene (exclusion filters, log routing) on either platform, not the free tier.

flashcards.q: Should a dependency's outage that degrades your SLI be excluded from SLO calculation?
flashcards.a: No by default -- SLOs and error budgets are deliberately cause-agnostic, measuring actual user-observed impact regardless of root cause. Excluding dependency failures risks the SLO no longer reflecting real user experience. If a dependency's failures distort the SLO meaningfully, the better fix is improving resilience (retries, fallbacks, circuit breakers) or renegotiating the SLO target, not quietly excluding inconvenient data.
